summary: Round 23 recheck, 28 Sep ~04:00-04:40Z. At the 04:06:33Z poll header, 47/48/49 were still PENDING and the best was exp70g 0.956. About 63 items rechecked in rounds 2-22 were skipped. Two of the three picks are the x138 knobs John Taylor disclosed in topic 743929 (round 22 logged them only); the third is the lab premise behind the whole low-score node-recovery family. All three were measured on CPU on the exp60 lab (56 clips). Nothing was built, pushed, submitted or committed. (A) READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.965 -> 0.94. The old value verdict (-0.001..+0.0005) and the round-17 upheld verdict were in-sample. The lab can see only the node cost: 6,696 band candidates (+0.60% nodes), 0 of them within 4 um of an annotated node. The out-of-sample reads are one display step each way (readmit added 0.947 -> 0.946; JT lowered it 0.958 -> 0.959). NEW VERDICT: the reason is corrected and the knob stays out of automatic slots (the W3/W4 knob ban). It is the best zero-code candidate for a slot that would otherwise go to the exp76e filler or stay empty, but only on a one-line user OK, public-only. (B) ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT 1.2 -> 0.4. R20-RC-B already voided the precision reasons, but the code confirms R11's 'no channel'. The motion relink replaces every ILP edge 1:1, with 0/56 raw-edge fallbacks in the lab. Appearance weight 0 makes an ILP fork's second child an orphan start either way. So JT's +0.001 came through his own ported post-processing, or is rounding, and does not carry over to our stack. STAYS CLOSED, with a new reason. (C) The premise that sub-threshold nodes are worthless ('readmitted/synthetic nodes match GT ~1%'; R17 'misses are misplaced, not absent'). In the lab, 99.5% of annotated nuclei that have a peak have it at >= 0.965. Readmitted nodes are 7-8x depleted near GT, and gapfill peak nodes are 0/1,049. This is detector memorisation, so the lab cannot sign any sub-threshold node lever in either direction. The premise is VOID as evidence. No pre-deadline action changes, but post-deadline node-recovery work needs an embryo-held-out bed, and lab-positive drops of readmit/gapfill nodes are suspect.

findings.what: READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.965 -> 0.94 (x138 knob; readmit = free low-detection peaks within 4 um of an open end/start after the first flow relink). OLD VERDICT: refuted on value (v3 v_metric-math_readmit-recall-knobs_value.json: 'only 424 end-anchored FN; band readmits +0.5-2% nodes, mostly linked -> -0.0004..-0.0015; net -0.001..+0.0005; public readmit step 0.947 -> 0.946'); v3 FINAL_REPORT (i) 'READMIT_MIN_SCORE in F1: -0.0015..+0.0007'; R17-RC-A kept it closed ('node levers flip by embryo'); round 22 logged JT's step as 'log only'. WHAT CHANGED: (1) John Taylor (public 0.959) reports this exact step on an x138 fork: 0.958 -> 0.959. Nodes moved < 1%, and his local annotated-edge Jaccard was unchanged ('0 of 2,212 edges changed'). (2) Measured today: the lab is structurally blind to this knob. On 56 exp60 clips, free peaks in [0.94, 0.965) within 4 um of an open end number 6,696 (+0.60% of 1,124,511 final nodes; 44b6 +1.09%, 6bba +0.32%). NONE of them lies within 4 um of an annotated GT node. The in-sample detector puts >= 0.965 on 99.5% of the annotated nuclei that have a peak (R23-RC-C). So any lab or local readout of this knob (the old -0.0015..+0.0007, JT's '0 of 2,212') measures only the node-count cost, about -0.0005 at +0.6% nodes. It cannot see the recall side, which exists only on unseen embryos. (3) Public and private are both unseen embryos for the detector. For a detector-score lever, the public board is therefore a better proxy for private than the lab, but it is ONE embryo, and the band population differs about 3x between our two train embryos. OUT-OF-SAMPLE EVIDENCE: two single display steps of opposite sign, on other bases. frontier947 chain + readmit at 0.965: 0.947 -> 0.946. JT's lowering to 0.94: 0.958 -> 0.959. Central ~0, spread about +-0.001. NEW VERDICT: the reason is corrected. It is not 'the lab says negative' but 'the lab cannot sign it; out-of-sample reads are split'. It stays out of every automatic slot: it is a knob rung, banned in W3/W4 by READ TABLE v2 (6) and W4 AMEND 2 (4), and no pre-registration covers it. It is, however, the most informative zero-code candidate for a slot that the W2 v4 (2)(v) branch would give to the exp76e filler or leave unused. exp76e (cap 6 + forkmid) nearly repeats probe 46 (exp70q, code 0). Realistic: public +0.000..+0.001, P(display +1 over BASE) ~0.2-0.3; private sign unknown, P(<0) ~0.4-0.5.

findings.what: ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT 1.2 -> 0.4 (JT's other disclosed step, 0.957 -> 0.958 on his x138 fork). OLD VERDICT: R11-RC-B kept it closed for five reasons: (1)-(3) in-sample exp12 fork precision 0.149 < post-insertion break-even 0.161, marginal precision lower still; (4) 'no channel: x138's relink is one-to-one and emits no ILP forks'; (5) no replay bed. Round 22 logged JT's step as 'ILP-division line closed (r11)'. WHAT CHANGED: R20-RC-B voided (1)-(3). Probe 45 showed that lab fork precision mis-signs public division adds (lab 0 TP / 4 FP vs public +0.002). JT gives a public +0.001 for this exact knob. RE-DERIVED on the code (exp70g filter_output_graph): whenever motion_relink_edges returns edges, it REPLACES the entire ILP edge list (edges = motion_edges; a 1:1 Hungarian per frame pair). ILP edges survive only when relink returns [] (a frame > MOTION_RELINK_MAX_FRAME_NODES 2600) or under _deadline_degrade. Lab final_stats over 56 clips: motion_relink_fallback_raw 0, skipped_large_frame 0, dropped_division_edges 0. So an ILP fork can never reach our output. The weight moves only (a) the ILP node set (<1% per JT) and (b) which pairs get the learned_edge_probs relink bonus. With ILP_APPEARANCE_WEIGHT 0.0, the second child of an ILP fork is an orphan start in either solution, so the orphan supply for safe divisions and DaughterNet insertion (the channel probe 45 moved) is essentially unchanged. JT's +0.001 therefore came through his own ported post-processing stage (base 0.957, unpublished), or is a rounding step. It does not carry over to our stack by mechanism. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED. The reason is replaced: not 'precision below break-even' (void since probe 45) but 'no output channel in x138: relink replaces all ILP edges, 0/56 fallbacks; appearance 0 makes fork children orphans anyway; JT's gain is base-specific'. It is not a filler candidate, and it is never stacked with R23-RC-A.

findings.what: The premise used to close or down-rank the low-score node-recovery family (readmit threshold, gapfill knobs, DoG / optional nodes / LoG shoulders, SimView readmit pool) and to up-rank node-drop levers. OLD VERDICTS: R11-d3 'synthetic and readmitted nodes match GT at about 1% (58/5,647; 29/2,968), so any variant only moves the node-count term'; R13NC-4 post-hoc bounds (readmit drop +0.00049, gapfill +0.00012); v3 simview-readmit-pool '+0.0002'; R17-RC-A (b) '71% of x138 misses have an unclaimed node at 7-10 um: the residual FN mass is misplaced nodes of seen nuclei, not absent peaks; adding nodes creates duplicates; the post-deadline lever is z-re-localisation'. WHAT CHANGED (measured today, 56 exp60 clips): (1) Detector saturation at annotated nuclei. The best pool peak within 3 um of a GT node is >= 0.965 for 85.7% (44b6) / 82.7% (6bba) of GT nodes, in [0.94, 0.965) for 0.03% / 0.05%, below 0.94 for 0.06% / 0.12%, and absent for 14.2% / 17.2%. Across ALL pool peaks, 4.0% / 1.4% fall in [0.94, 0.965). Annotated nuclei are therefore ~30-130x depleted in the sub-threshold band. (2) Node classes, share within 4 um of a GT node: plain 0.76% / 4.98%; readmitted 0.09% / 0.68% (7-8x depleted); gap_synthetic 0.36% / 1.58%; gap2_synthetic 0.38% / 1.57%; gapfill_peak 0/719 and 0/330. The detectors were trained on all 199 train videos, including these clips. In the lab, every annotated nucleus therefore already carries a >= 0.965 peak and is claimed upstream, and a node recovered from sub-threshold evidence can only land on an unannotated cell. The same saturation forces the in-sample miss anatomy toward 'misplaced, not absent'. NEW VERDICT: the premise is an in-sample artifact and is VOID as value evidence in both directions. Adding such nodes looks like pure node cost. Dropping readmit or gapfill nodes looks like a free gain; this is the pattern of leaf prune (lab +0.0005/+0.0006 -> LB tie, probe 27; exp70a lp30 NEU) and the readmit-drop sibling. The family stays closed before the deadline for its own reasons (R8 for new stages, the runtime gate for DoG, the knob ban for thresholds; R23-RC-A is the only exception, on a user OK). R17's post-deadline direction ('z-re-localisation, not adding nodes') drops from a conclusion to one of two open hypotheses.
